ministries.alt: Officials gathered around a world map

ministries.name: Ministry of Social Affairs
ministries.alt: Workers gathered in a municipal office

rounds.title: The first test
rounds.subtitle: A new cabinet inherits a city already under pressure.

education.title: The thinking city
education.brief: AI tutors have spread through every school. Results are rising, but teachers warn that pupils are learning to obey answers rather than understand them.
education.question: What place should AI have in the classroom?

choices.title: Open every system
choices.detail: Give every pupil unrestricted access.
choices.result: Access expands overnight, but confidence in public schools fractures.

choices.title: Keep a human in the room
choices.detail: Fund supervised use, training and audits.
choices.result: The programme is costly, but teachers turn machines into tools.

choices.title: Ban it from schools
choices.detail: Protect the old curriculum.
choices.result: Classrooms regain their rhythm while wealthy families buy the advantage elsewhere.

education.title: A school for every district
education.brief: Population growth has filled classrooms beyond capacity. The treasury can fund buildings quickly or improve teaching slowly.
education.question: Where should the education budget go?

choices.title: Build now
choices.detail: Open modular schools in every crowded district.
choices.result: Capacity rises quickly; quality varies from street to street.

choices.title: Invest in teachers
choices.detail: Raise pay and reduce class sizes over time.
choices.result: The waiting list remains, but the profession begins to recover.

choices.title: Invite private partners
choices.detail: Let companies finance new academies.
choices.result: New schools open with new sponsors—and new inequalities.

foreign.title: The distant front
foreign.brief: A neighbouring state asks for protection as an enemy army crosses its frontier. Allies demand resolve; the streets fear another generation sent away.
foreign.question: How far will the city enter the war?

choices.title: Intervene openly
choices.detail: Send forces and make the alliance credible.
choices.result: The city keeps its promise. Casualty lists arrive before the speeches end.

choices.title: Arm them quietly
choices.detail: Provide intelligence, medicine and weapons.
choices.result: The front holds. Official neutrality becomes a useful fiction.

choices.title: Close the border
choices.detail: Declare neutrality and preserve the city.
choices.result: The gates close as refugees gather on the other side.

foreign.title: The refugee train
foreign.brief: The first trains from the frontier arrive before dawn. Municipal shelters are full and cameras are waiting.
foreign.question: What promise will you make at the station?

choices.title: Offer sanctuary
choices.detail: Accept arrivals and requisition housing.
choices.result: Thousands find safety; the city absorbs a sudden, visible strain.

choices.title: Share the burden
choices.detail: Negotiate quotas with allied cities.
choices.result: Diplomacy works slowly, distributing both people and responsibility.

choices.title: Temporary admission
choices.detail: Open camps outside the city limits.
choices.result: The crisis is contained, not resolved.

interior.title: Eyes in the street
interior.brief: Sabotage and street violence follow the war debate home. The security service offers certainty—if it may watch everyone.
interior.question: What kind of order will you impose?

choices.title: Build the watchful city
choices.detail: Approve mass surveillance and predictive arrests.
choices.result: Attacks fall. So do private conversations and public trust.

choices.title: People, not cameras
choices.detail: Fund mediators, services and accountable patrols.
choices.result: Order returns unevenly, neighbourhood by neighbourhood.

choices.title: Declare an emergency
choices.detail: Impose curfews and extraordinary powers.
choices.result: The streets empty; temporary powers settle into habit.

interior.title: A march on the square
interior.brief: Two rival demonstrations are converging on the same civic square. Police warn that they cannot guarantee calm.
interior.question: How will you police the protest?

choices.title: Protect both marches
choices.detail: Divide the square and deploy trained stewards.
choices.result: The day is tense, loud and mostly peaceful.

choices.title: Ban the demonstrations
choices.detail: Close the square before crowds arrive.
choices.result: The square stays empty; anger moves into side streets.

choices.title: Back the loyalists
choices.detail: Allow only the pro-government march.
choices.result: The cabinet gains a cheering crowd and loses its claim to neutrality.

social.title: The price of labour
social.brief: Automation has made the city richer and its citizens less necessary. Employers promise abundance. Workers ask who it is for.
social.question: What future of work will the city finance?

choices.title: Protect every job
choices.detail: Subsidise wages and slow automation.
choices.result: Pay packets survive while the treasury takes the strain.

choices.title: Automate without apology
choices.detail: Let industry replace labour and reinvest.
choices.result: Production surges. The unemployed watch from outside the gates.

choices.title: Create work worth doing
choices.detail: Fund housing, care and restoration.
choices.result: The city spends deeply and becomes visibly more liveable.

social.title: The rent ultimatum
social.brief: Rents have risen for eleven consecutive months. Tenant unions threaten a citywide strike.
social.question: How will you answer the housing crisis?

choices.title: Freeze rents
choices.detail: Cap increases for two years.
choices.result: Tenants breathe again; new construction slows.

choices.title: Build public housing
choices.detail: Borrow heavily and start construction.
choices.result: Cranes appear across the city alongside a larger public debt.

choices.title: Trust the market
choices.detail: Relax planning rules and offer tax relief.
choices.result: Investment returns first; affordable homes may follow later.

rounds.title: The aftershocks
rounds.subtitle: Every promise now collides with the choices made by another ministry.

education.title: The missing cohort
education.brief: War, displacement and housing pressure have pushed thousands of children out of regular schooling.
education.question: How will you bring them back?

choices.title: A national catch-up year
choices.detail: Guarantee tutoring, meals and transport.
choices.result: Attendance rebounds at a price the treasury cannot hide.

choices.title: Digital classrooms
choices.detail: Issue devices and teach remotely.
choices.result: Coverage grows quickly; the least stable homes fall furthest behind.

choices.title: Prioritise examinations
choices.detail: Concentrate resources on graduating pupils.
choices.result: Results stabilise while younger children wait.

education.title: The civic curriculum
education.brief: After months of polarisation, the cabinet asks schools to strengthen democratic resilience.
education.question: What should children be taught about the crisis?

choices.title: Teach the controversy
choices.detail: Publish evidence and let pupils debate it.
choices.result: Classrooms become difficult, serious democratic spaces.

choices.title: A common national story
choices.detail: Issue one approved civic curriculum.
choices.result: The message is clear; its silences are clearer.

choices.title: Keep politics outside
choices.detail: Return strictly to core subjects.
choices.result: Schools grow quieter, not necessarily wiser.

foreign.title: The peace table
foreign.brief: A ceasefire is possible, but only if the city sits across from a government it has publicly condemned.
foreign.question: What will you trade for peace?

choices.title: Negotiate directly
choices.detail: Accept political risk and open talks.
choices.result: The guns quiet while accusations of betrayal fill the chamber.

choices.title: Demand guarantees
choices.detail: Wait for allies to underwrite a settlement.
choices.result: The coalition holds; fighting continues another month.

choices.title: Seek total victory
choices.detail: Reject talks and escalate support.
choices.result: The city looks resolute as the human cost rises.

foreign.title: The reconstruction fund
foreign.brief: Allies propose a vast recovery fund. Joining means a decade of financial commitments and a seat at the table.
foreign.question: Will the city sign?

choices.title: Lead the fund
choices.detail: Contribute generously and shape the programme.
choices.result: Influence grows abroad while reserves shrink at home.

choices.title: Join cautiously
choices.detail: Make a limited, conditional contribution.
choices.result: The city keeps a voice without owning the project.

choices.title: Rebuild at home first
choices.detail: Decline and protect national reserves.
choices.result: The treasury recovers as diplomatic invitations thin out.

interior.title: The leaked files
interior.brief: Documents show that emergency surveillance reached journalists and opposition councillors.
interior.question: How will you respond?

choices.title: Publish and investigate
choices.detail: Release the files and appoint an independent judge.
choices.result: Trust begins to recover; senior officials begin to resign.

choices.title: Reform in private
choices.detail: Limit the programme without admitting wrongdoing.
choices.result: The machinery shrinks quietly and suspicion remains.

choices.title: Defend the service
choices.detail: Call the leak a threat to national security.
choices.result: The apparatus survives, protected by a harder political line.

interior.title: The night of fires
interior.brief: Coordinated arson strikes public buildings. Evidence is incomplete; pressure for arrests is immediate.
interior.question: What standard of certainty will you require?

choices.title: Wait for evidence
choices.detail: Protect due process despite public anger.
choices.result: Investigators move slowly and build a case that may endure.

choices.title: Targeted emergency arrests
choices.detail: Detain named suspects under judicial review.
choices.result: The network is disrupted with limited collateral damage.

choices.title: Sweep the districts
choices.detail: Arrest broadly and restore visible control.
choices.result: The fires stop; whole neighbourhoods remember the raids.

social.title: The winter ledger
social.brief: Energy bills, food prices and unemployment now converge. The welfare system cannot answer every claim.
social.question: Who receives protection first?

choices.title: Universal relief
choices.detail: Cap bills for every household.
choices.result: The measure is simple, popular and extremely expensive.

choices.title: Target the poorest
choices.detail: Means-test cash support and debt relief.
choices.result: Help reaches those in greatest need after a maze of forms.

choices.title: Protect employment
choices.detail: Subsidise employers who retain workers.
choices.result: Jobs survive, though struggling households wait for wages.

social.title: The social contract
social.brief: The crisis is easing. Unions and employers want a permanent settlement for the automated economy.
social.question: What bargain will define the next decade?

choices.title: A shorter working week
choices.detail: Share productive gains through time.
choices.result: Life outside work expands while firms reorganise.

choices.title: Universal basic income
choices.detail: Replace fragmented benefits with one payment.
choices.result: Security becomes universal and the fiscal argument begins anew.

choices.title: Skills in exchange for support
choices.detail: Tie benefits to retraining programmes.
choices.result: The policy rewards mobility and disciplines those who cannot move.
